h1: Cylinder storage temperature and safe hot-water delivery
title: Cylinder Temperature & Hot-Water Safety | G3 Guide
description: Understand cylinder storage temperature and safe hot-water delivery with clear model-aware information and practical questions for your cylinder engineer.
answer: Storage temperature, outlet blending, scalding risk and water hygiene must be considered together. Avoid arbitrary temperature changes to resolve bills or discomfort.

sections.heading: The key distinction
paragraphs: HSE landlord guidance gives storage at 60°C as an example control measure within proportionate legionella risk management. Manufacturer instructions describe the appliance control range and safety arrangements. Neither should be turned into a universal instruction for a householder to open controls.

sections.heading: Apply the information to the installed system
paragraphs: Safe delivery can involve appropriate mixing at points of use, particularly where scalding risk matters. A competent assessment should distinguish stored-water temperature from outlet temperature and take the building use and installed strategy into account.

sections.heading: A practical next question
paragraphs: Gather the full model, heating method, recent symptoms and available paperwork. Discuss the scope with a person competent for the actual work. Technical information here supports that conversation and is not a substitute for manufacturer instructions or individual system assessment.

faqs.question: Is the cylinder storage temperature necessarily the temperature delivered at every tap?
faqs.answer: No. Blending, distribution and outlet controls can change delivery; storage hygiene and scalding precautions need to be considered together.
